elections.notes: The party rows add up to 6,784,739 votes, 432,203 fewer than the 7,216,942 valid votes the table states; its footnote says the official results are inconsistent. pct is the table's share of the party total. Independents won the most seats (85, flagged as winner); the largest party was the National Association (55). The table's "Other parties" row (10 seats) is counted in Others. The table has no seat-change column. Region winners: most constituency seats in each province or city, from the article's by-city/province table. No winner for North Gyeongsang (tie: National Association 11, Independents 11); Jeju (tie: National Association 1, Independents 1). Not yet separate units at this election: Busan, Daegu, Incheon, Gwangju, Daejeon, Ulsan, Sejong.

elections.note: A third of seats appointed by the president

source.name: Wikipedia, citing Nohlen, Grotz and Hartmann, Elections in Asia: A Data Handbook, Volume II (2001)

elections.notes: A null change means the table shows "New" or no figure. Two-thirds of the seats were elected in two-member constituencies; the table adds a row for the 73 presidential appointees (nominated by Park Chung Hee and confirmed by the National Conference for Unification), without votes. The Democratic Republican Party and the appointees both hold 73 seats; the party is flagged as winner. Region winners: most constituency seats in each province or city, from the article's by-city/province table. No winner for Busan (tie: Democratic Republican Party 4, New Democratic Party 4); South Chungcheong (tie: Democratic Republican Party 6, New Democratic Party 6); North Jeolla (tie: Democratic Republican Party 4, New Democratic Party 4, Independents 4); Jeju (tie: Democratic Republican Party 1, Independents 1). Not yet separate units at this election: Daegu, Incheon, Gwangju, Daejeon, Ulsan, Sejong.

elections.notes: Two-thirds of the seats were elected in two-member constituencies; the table adds a row for the 77 presidential appointees (nominated by Park Chung Hee and confirmed by the National Conference for Unification), without votes. The appointees are the largest group, so they carry the winner flag; of the elected seats the Democratic Republican Party won the most (68) while the New Democratic Party won the most votes. Region winners: most constituency seats in each province or city, from the article's by-city/province table. No winner for Jeju (tie: Democratic Republican Party 1, Independents 1). Not yet separate units at this election: Daegu, Incheon, Gwangju, Daejeon, Ulsan, Sejong.

elections.note: Two-thirds of 92 national seats to the largest party

source.name: Wikipedia, citing Nohlen, Grotz and Hartmann, Elections in Asia: A Data Handbook, Volume II (2001)

elections.notes: A null change means the table shows "New" or no figure. 184 seats were elected in two-member constituencies; the other 92 were shared among parties with five or more constituency seats, two-thirds of them to the largest party (per the article). Region winners: most constituency seats in each province or city, from the article's by-city/province table. In North Gyeongsang (22 vs 26), South Gyeongsang (24 vs 20) the party seats do not add up to the row's total, but the leader's margin is larger than the gap. No winner for North Chungcheong (party seats add up to 9, the row total is 8); North Jeolla (party seats add up to 13, the row total is 14). Not yet separate units at this election: Daegu, Incheon, Gwangju, Daejeon, Ulsan, Sejong.
